# Configuration: atlas.json

<!-- Generated by Tools/Update-ConfigDoc.ps1 from schemas/atlas.schema.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Settings for Atlas. Each key has exactly one place (x-scope): "project" in atlas.json in the project folder (Atlas › Project settings), "global" in %APPDATA%\Atlas\settings.json for all projects (Tools › Options › Atlas). "both" in both places: the global file applies to all projects, atlas.json overrides per member (rules: per rule). A key in the wrong place is ignored and reported.

Each key has exactly one place (column "Place"): project keys live in `atlas.json` in the project folder (in the plugin *Atlas › Project settings*), global keys in `%APPDATA%\Atlas\settings.json` for all projects (in the plugin *Tools › Options › Atlas*). Exception `rules`: check rules work in both places, globally for all projects, `atlas.json` overrides per rule. A key in the wrong place is ignored and reported as a warning. Missing keys take the default value. In the IDE the running IDE determines the Delphi version (`delphiVersion` does not apply there). The check rules are described in [Regeln.md](../Regeln.md) (German). The German version of this page is [Konfiguration.md](../Konfiguration.md).

`atlas.json` lives in the repository and applies to everyone in the team (#486). Credentials (keys such as `token`, `password`, `user` on any level, addresses such as `https://user:pw@…` or `?token=…`) and absolute paths (drive or UNC) in the path settings (`project`, `testUnits.folder`, `testUnits.project`, `exclude`, `index.exclude`, `overrides[].files`) are ignored when reading and reported as a warning. Glob patterns from the project folder (`/Generated/**`) and relative paths (`..\Tests`) stay allowed. The global `settings.json` is personal and exempt from this. The team settings of the plugin live in the separate project file `.atlas`.

The language of findings, light bulb, hover and settings follows the IDE (#1458): `language` `""` takes the language of the client (Delphi IDE: its language, otherwise English), `"de"` and `"en"` fix it. `AtlasServer --check` takes `--locale de|en`.

## Keys

| Key | Place | Type | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `delphiVersion` | global (settings.json) | string | – | e.g. `"37.0"`, `"23.0"` | Delphi version as product number ("13", "12", "10.4") or as in the registry ("37.0" for Delphi 13, "23.0" for Delphi 12). Empty: matching the ProjectVersion of the .dproj, otherwise the next higher one, otherwise the newest installed version. If the configured version is not installed, the server log warns with the location in settings.json and the automatic choice applies. Without any installation (Linux, CI) the configured version or the one matching the ProjectVersion applies, otherwise the newest known version, only for CompilerVersion and VERxxx. In the IDE the running IDE always applies. |
| `minDelphiVersion` | project (atlas.json) | string | – | e.g. `"23.0"`, `"22.0"` | Oldest Delphi version the project must compile with, as product number ("12", "11") or as in the registry ("23.0"). Atlas reports language features of newer versions (rule language-feature, e.g. "is not" or the if expression with "12"), and code actions, slash commands and formatting do not produce them. The older of this and the selected version (delphiVersion or the running IDE) applies. Empty: only the selected version. |
| `language` | global (settings.json) | string | `""` | `""`, `"de"`, `"en"` | Language of findings, code actions, hovers, previews and server messages (#1458): "de" or "en". Empty: like the IDE (the plugin sends its language in initializationOptions.locale, other editors in initialize.locale), otherwise English. AtlasServer --check takes --locale before this setting. |
| `encoding` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"utf-8"` | e.g. `"utf-8"`, `"windows-1252"`, `"windows-1250"` | Default encoding for files without BOM when detection does not decide (pure ASCII, invalid UTF-8): "utf-8" or an ANSI code page like "windows-1250". Binary forms are never changed. |
| `project` | project (atlas.json) | string | – |  | Project file (.dproj) relative to this folder. Empty: search automatically. |
| `config` | project (atlas.json) | string | – | e.g. `"Debug"`, `"Release"` | Build configuration, e.g. Debug or Release. |
| `platform` | project (atlas.json) | string | – | e.g. `"Win32"`, `"Win64"` | Target platform. |
| `rules` | global and project | object | – |  | Configure rules individually: rule id → severity or object with "severity" and options. Main switch per group of the settings page (#909): "group:<group>": "off" turns off all rules of the group (groups see Regeln.md, e.g. "group:threads"). The group “Compiler ahead” also takes an object (#1024): "group:compiler": {"severity": "off", "typeLevel": "off"}; "typeLevel": "off" turns off only the rules of level T that need expression types (levels see Regeln.md). The confidence of a finding limits the severity here too: with medium confidence a finding stays at most a warning, with low confidence at most a hint, even with "error". |
| `profile` | project (atlas.json) |  | `"standard"` | e.g. `"fast"`, `"strict"` | Rule profile: standard, fast (only bugs and vulnerabilities), strict (experimental rules on, minConfidence low), security, style or a custom one from "profiles". As an object separately for editor and command line. |
| `profiles` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Custom rule profiles: name → { "extends": built-in or custom profile, "categories": only these categories, "rules": rule id → severity }. |
| `ruleChecks` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Rule checks in the LSP session (#1454): module switch "Rule checks" of the plugin (Tools › Options › Atlas › Rule checks). Off = the server checks no rules in the IDE session; only syntax errors and compiler messages appear. AtlasServer --check and the MCP tool keep checking according to atlas.json. |
| `overrides` | project (atlas.json) | array<object> | – |  | Path rules: severities for files that match one of the glob patterns, e.g. downgrade tests or generated code. Rule id "*" stands for all rules; later entries take precedence. |
| `excludeTests` | global and project | boolean | `false` |  | Do not check test units and test projects (uses DUnitX.TestFramework, TestFramework or TestInsight.*). Switchable globally for all projects; an atlas.json that names the key takes precedence. |
| `testProfile` | project (atlas.json) | string | – | e.g. `"fast"` | Rule profile for test units and test projects; empty: like "profile". |
| `compiler` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Compiler connection: command line compiler (dcc32/dcc64). Without it a running RAD Studio with Atlas builds (tool build_project). |
| `vcs` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Version control (Git, SVN) for changed files, branch and revision. |
| `completion` | mixed, see below | object | – |  | Code completion. |
| `refactoring` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Code that Atlas generates. |
| `usesCommand` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | A line "/uses Unit1, Unit2" is deleted after Enter and the units go into the matching uses. |
| `completeBlocks` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Typing aids that add code while typing. |
| `metrics` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Metrics at all: false turns off the metrics above methods (codeLens.metrics) and all rules metric-* for all projects. A project overrides this per rule by setting it explicitly in atlas.json under "rules", e.g. "metric-method-length": "warning". |
| `experimental` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Experimental features (#834): risky or not yet mature, can be turned off, marked as "Experimental" and off after installation. |
| `slashCommands` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Slash commands: a line starting with /name is executed after Enter and disappears. After / completion suggests all commands. |
| `sortUses` | project (atlas.json) | boolean string | `false` | `true`, `false`, `"alphabetic"`, `"namespace"` | "Organize uses" (source.organizeImports, e.g. on save) sorts the uses: true or "alphabetic" alphabetically, "namespace" grouped by namespace (System, Vcl, ... and units without namespace last). Caution: the order determines the initialization of the units. |
| `usesKeep` | project (atlas.json) | array<string> | `` |  | Units that "Remove unused uses" never removes, in addition to all units with an initialization section. |
| `deadCode` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Dead code: elements that count as used although their name does not appear in the code (RTTI, serialization, plugins). Applies to unused-private-member, unused-public-member and unused-declaration, in addition to the options keepAttributes and keepPatterns of the rules. |
| `dfmPropertyRules` | project (atlas.json) | array<object> | `` |  | Property rules for form files: requirements for component properties, reported as dfm-property on the field of the component in the unit. Properties not stored count with their default value. |
| `memoryBudgetMb` | global (settings.json) | integer | `768` | 0… | Upper limit for the symbol index in memory in MB. Above it first library units (RTL, VCL) are kept compact (interface symbols only), then the usages of project units are swapped out (they stay in the cache on disk) and finally project units are kept compact. 0: unlimited. |
| `index` | mixed, see below | object | – |  | Scope of the symbol index. Default: all projects of the project group, all units of the project search paths and all units of the library and search paths of the Delphi installation, even if no unit uses them. Order: active project, other projects, search paths, library; everything in the background, the library from the shared cache. |
| `architecture` | mixed, see below | object | – |  | Architecture overview from the index: central units, subsystems, cycles and cross connections in the window "Atlas Architecture", as a report (Markdown or HTML, also AtlasServer --architecture) and in the MCP tool get_architecture. |
| `query` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Code queries over the index (#1351): a small language such as "classes where inherits TForm and methods > 40 order by methods desc" in the window "Atlas Query", in the MCP tool query_code and with AtlasServer --check <target> --query. Fields and numbers come from index, metrics, uses graph, form files and call hierarchy (the same as get_metrics and find_unused_code). |
| `queries` | project (atlas.json) | array<object> | `` | e.g. `{"name":"grosse-formulare","query":"classes where inherits TForm and methods > 40","failIfAny":true,"severity":"warning","message":"{name} hat {methods} Methoden"}` | Saved code queries (#1351) for the window "Atlas Query", query_code and AtlasServer --query @name. With failIfAny every hit becomes a finding of the rule query:<name> in the editor, with --check and in SARIF; baseline, suppressions and rules act as for other rules. |
| `hotspots` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Hotspots: units and methods that are changed often and are complex at the same time (changes from Git or SVN in the period × cognitive complexity), with trend compared to three months ago and change coupling (units without uses edge that are often changed together). Window "Atlas Hotspots", report (AtlasServer --hotspots <file.html\|.md\|.json>) and MCP tool get_hotspots. Library units and architecture.exclude do not count; the version control comes from vcs.provider. |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | global (settings.json) | integer | `10000` | 1000… | Time limit for requests in milliseconds. Requests running longer are cancelled and reported in the log. |
| `server` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Crash cases of the server: if a request crashes with an unexpected exception or the watchdog cancels it, the server saves a reproducible case under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\crash (request, snapshot of the file, settings without credentials, call stack, wiederholen.cmd; at most 20). No network access. |
| `diagnostics` | mixed, see below | object | – |  | Anonymized diagnostic log of the server (per request duration, result and reason code, per run start and end with reason). It contains no paths, no project, unit or identifier names and no source code and can be passed on via "Export diagnostic log". |
| `highlight` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Highlight related keywords when the cursor is on one of them. |
| `inlayHints` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Inlay hints in the editor. |
| `codeLens` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Code lens in the editor. |
| `smartIndent` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Indentation while typing (#1827): after Enter Atlas computes where the cursor belongs, with the same block logic as format.reindent. Atlas never inserts end; (the IDE's block completion does that); only whitespace changes, and for a string the quote and +. Width of one level and tabs follow format or .editorconfig. |
| `suggestions` | project (atlas.json) | object | – | e.g. `{"patterns":[{"after":"Log.Enter","insert":["try","  $|","finally","  Log.Leave;","end;"]}]}` | Learned suggestions (#1890): after a trigger such as X := TFoo.Create; or L.BeginUpdate; the plugin suggests as grey ghost text what usually follows in the project (try … finally X.Free; end;). The switches and thresholds live in the plugin settings (suggestions.*). This holds the team's house rules. |
| `classCompletion` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Class completion (#1834): comment above a class section in the implementation part, order and content of new method bodies from the action "Create missing method bodies", /impl and method ordering (editor.methodPlacement in the plugin). |
| `references` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Accuracy of usages, call hierarchy and rename: besides the certain (uniquely resolved) places, inferred ones appear with a reason, for example calls via an interface or in an inactive {$IFDEF} branch. Rename only changes certain places and lists the inferred ones. |
| `navigation` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Navigation through the code: path between two symbols or units via calls, fields, interfaces, inheritance and uses (plugin command "Path between symbols…", MCP tool find_path) and impact analysis: what is affected if I change a symbol? Callers, references, overrides, interface implementations and form bindings by level, plus the affected tests (plugin command "Show impact", MCP tool get_impact). |
| `hints` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Display of XMLDoc comments (///) and rationales (// WHY: …, #1123) in the hover tooltip and in the detail panel of the completion of the IDE plugin. The server always prepares the documentation completely; the values only control the display. Without a value the values from Tools › Options › Third Party › Atlas apply. |
| `directives` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Help in compiler directives: completion and hover for directives such as {$R+} or {$WARN …} and for conditional symbols in {$IFDEF}, {$IFNDEF}, {$IF Defined(…)}, {$DEFINE} and {$UNDEF}. |
| `stringLiteral` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Code actions "As string literal" and "Copy as plain text". |
| `memberOrder` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Code action "Order class members": order of the visibility sections and of the members in them. |
| `testUnits` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Create test units and switch between unit and test unit: name pattern, folder of new test units and test project. |
| `tests` | mixed, see below | object | – |  | Affected tests of a change: determine the changed routines, types and constants from the difference to the base (Git or SVN), follow their impact and only name the DUnitX tests that reach them (command line --affected-tests, MCP tool get_affected_tests, plugin command "Run affected tests"). |
| `testLists` | project (atlas.json) | array<object> | – |  | Test lists in the “Atlas Tests” window (#2167), for everyone in the project: fixed lists (“tests”: names as in DUnitX, unit, unit.fixture or unit.fixture.method) and dynamic ones (“rules”, combined with “and”: category is or is not, unit or fixture matches a pattern with * and ?, state failed, not run or outdated). New tests that match belong to the list without further ado. Edited in the window; lists “only for me” are not stored here but with the plugin. |
| `minConfidence` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"medium"` | `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"` | Hide rule hits below this confidence. |
| `fix` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Bulk fix (--fix, MCP fix_findings, "Fix all safe hits …" in the window "Atlas Check"): only applies safe fixes of rules with safeFix in the catalog. |
| `exclude` | project (atlas.json) | array<string> | – | e.g. `["ThirdParty/**","Generated/*.pas"]` | Folders and files that are not checked (glob patterns relative to this folder: *, **, ?). |
| `mcp` | mixed, see below | object | – | e.g. `{"disabledTools":["rename_symbol","apply_code_action"]}`, `{"globalSettings":false}`, `{"prompts":true,"promptLanguage":"en"}` | MCP mode (--mcp) for AI assistants. |
| `format` | project (atlas.json) | object | – |  | Formatting (format document and selection). Values set here take precedence over .editorconfig. |
| `tasks` | global and project | array<object> | – |  | Project tasks (#900): commands of the project that the plugin starts via command palette, menu Atlas › Tasks, key, status field or quick action; the output goes to the tab "Atlas Tasks", detected locations as findings in the problem list and editor. Project before global for the same name. Variables in command, args, cwd and env: ${projectDir}, ${groupDir}, ${file}, ${fileDir}, ${config}, ${platform}, ${BDS}. |
| `issues` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Issue tracker in the plugin (Tools › Options › Atlas › Issue tracker, area "My issues"). Personal, therefore only in settings.json; the section tracker of the project file .atlas applies alongside for the team. |
| `logLevel` | global (settings.json) | string | `"info"` | `"debug"`, `"info"`, `"warning"`, `"error"` | Minimum level of the messages in the output window and in the log file. Applies from the next start; the command line option --log-level takes precedence. |
| `logFile` | global (settings.json) | string | `""` |  | Optional log file of the server (rotation at 10 MB). Applies from the next start; --log takes precedence. |
| `traceFile` | global (settings.json) | string | `""` |  | Optional recording of all JSON messages for troubleshooting. Applies from the next start; --trace takes precedence. |

## ruleChecks

| Key | Place | Type | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ruleChecks.enabled` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Main switch: false = no rule checks in the LSP session (notice at start and on every change); --check and MCP unchanged. |

## compiler

| Key | Place | Type | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compiler.onSave` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `false` |  | After saving a source file compile the project in the background and show the messages. Only with the command line compiler. |
| `compiler.backend` | global (settings.json) | string | `"auto"` | `"auto"`, `"dcc"`, `"off"` | Way to the compiler. auto: Atlas first detects per Delphi installation whether dcc32/dcc64 exists and is usable (the Starter and Community Edition print a license text instead of compiling), remembers it and then takes dcc, otherwise off. dcc: only the command line compiler. off: Atlas never compiles itself. If no compiler is usable, Atlas reports it once with reason and way out, shows it in the status (atlas.server.status), and the command “Compile project” answers with the reason. An old value "ide" counts as off, an old entry ideCommand is skipped. |

## vcs

| Key | Place | Type | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vcs.provider` | global (settings.json) | string | `"auto"` | `"auto"`, `"git"`, `"svn"`, `"off"` | auto: by the working copy found (.git or .svn, the nearest one applies, on a tie Git). git or svn: only this kind. off: without version control. Git and SVN through the command line (git or svn, TortoiseSVN with command line tools is enough); if the program is missing, Atlas reports it once and continues without version information. |
| `vcs.git` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Program git (#1285): path = path to git.exe, empty = search automatically. |
| `vcs.svn` | global (settings.json) | object | – |  | Program svn (#1285): path = path to svn.exe, empty = search automatically. |
| `vcs.projects` | global (settings.json) | array<object> | `` |  | Personal kind and main branch per Delphi project (#1286). The section vcs of the .atlas applies (per field), otherwise the row for exactly this .dproj, then the one of the opened .groupproj, then the longest matching folder, otherwise vcs.provider. For a folder (change markers) .dproj and .groupproj rows apply to their folder, the longest match wins. |
| `vcs.timeoutSeconds` | global (settings.json) | integer | `15` | 1…300 | Time limit per call of git or svn in seconds (#1285); after it Atlas ends the process. Calls with their own shorter limit (welcome page 1 s) keep theirs; creating a branch and pull take the larger of this value and 30 s. |

## completion

| Key | Place | Type | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `completion.matching` | global (settings.json) | string | `"fuzzy"` | `"fuzzy"`, `"prefix"` | Choice of suggestions: fuzzy (subsequences, abbreviations like TSL for TStringList) or only by prefix, in case an editor filters strictly afterwards. |
| `completion.interfaceSection` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"public"` | `"private"`, `"protected"`, `"public"` | Section of the class into which “Implement interface” writes the declarations of missing interface methods. |
| `completion.senderCast` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"as"` | `"as"`, `"cast"` | Form of the type cast when a member of the assigned components is chosen after Sender.: "as" writes (Sender as TButton), "cast" writes TButton(Sender). |
| `completion.offerTryFinally` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | After accepting a constructor in "List := TStringList.Create;" offer to wrap the following code in try…finally with freeing. |
| `completion.freeStyle` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"free"` | `"free"`, `"freeAndNil"` | Freeing in the finally of “Secure freeing”: "free" writes List.Free, "freeAndNil" writes FreeAndNil(List). |
| `completion.keywords` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Suggest keywords that fit the place (in statements begin, try …, in the class body property, private …, after ":" string, array …) as soon as a character is typed. |
| `completion.postfixTemplates` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Offer postfix templates after an expression: List.for becomes for var Item in List do, FCustomer.notnil becomes if Assigned(FCustomer) then, plus tryf, ifa, fmt, nil, not, if, forin, free, try, var, exit and your own templates with "postfix: true". |
| `completion.genericConstraints` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | After "TObjectList<" only suggest types that satisfy the constraints of the type parameter (class, record, constructor, interface or class), with the heading "T: class · classes only" and the hidden kinds in the footer. |
| `completion.createAccessors` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | After read or write of a property declaration offer "Create field FName", "Create GetName" and "Create SetName" at the top of the list: field in the private section (strict private if the class uses it), methods in the section given by accessorSection, setter with change check. |
| `completion.accessorSection` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"private"` | `"private"`, `"protected"` | Section of the class into which "Create GetName" and "Create SetName" write the accessor methods. |
| `completion.resourceStrings` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Ctrl+Space in a string literal offers "Extract as resourcestring": name from the first words (S + CamelCase, umlauts replaced), entry in the resourcestring section; if the text already exists, also "Use existing". Not in constants, attributes, case labels and parameter defaults. |
| `completion.resourceStringUnit` | project (atlas.json) | string | `""` |  | Unit whose interface part receives extracted resourcestrings (for example App.Texts); it is added to uses when needed. Empty: implementation part of the own unit. |
| `completion.typeConversion` | global (settings.json) | string | `"off"` | `"off"`, `"helper"`, `"function"` | **Experimental (off by default; only active with `experimental.enabled`).** If an entry does not fit the expected type (assignment, argument), Atlas suggests the usual conversion as an extra entry directly above the original, for example Count.ToString for a string assignment: number, Boolean, date and enumeration to string, string to number. helper: helper style (X.ToString, X.ToInteger) where one exists, otherwise function; function: function style (IntToStr(X), StrToInt(X)); off: off. Required units are added to uses. For floating point to integer only a hint on Round and Trunc in the detail panel. |
| `completion.assignAllFields` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `false` |  | **Experimental (off by default; only active with `experimental.enabled`).** After a record or class expression with a dot at the start of a statement (Opts.) "Assign all fields (n)" is at the very top: one line Opts.Field := placeholder per public writable field and property, in declaration order, with 0, '', False, nil or the first enumeration value as default in placeholder mode. Fields that the following lines already assign are left out. With more than 15 fields a list with check boxes comes first. |
| `completion.usesDetails` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | In the uses section: hide units already used (the footer names them), group units by project, RTL/VCL and third party, complete short forms to the namespace (Classes → System.Classes), mark units from the other section with "already in interface part" or "… implementation part" and units with circular reference in the interface part; path and the first exported types in the detail panel. Off: all units of the index as a plain list. |
| `completion.inheritedCall` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | After "inherited " first offer the complete call of the ancestor method of the same name with the parameters of the own method (label "same parameters"), then its other overloads, in constructors and destructors also the other constructors or destructors of the ancestors. Abstract ancestor methods are missing, the footer names them. In functions accepting adds "Result := " if nothing precedes inherited on the line. Off: only the names of the ancestor methods. |
| `completion.attributes` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | After "[" before a type, method, field, property or parameter declaration only offer attribute classes (descendants of TCustomAttribute) without the suffix Attribute; known ones first (DUnitX Test, TestCase, TestFixture, Setup, TearDown, JSONName, JSONMarshalled, the compiler attributes weak, unsafe, volatile, Ref), on the right the parameters of the constructor or the unit, from units not yet used with a uses entry. After "(" the parameter hint shows the constructor. Off: the ordinary list. |
| `completion.anonymousMethods` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | If an argument or an assignment expects a method reference type (reference to procedure/function, e.g. TProc, TFunc<T>, TPredicate<T> or your own), offer a skeleton with matching signature at the top of the list: procedure(const Value: TCustomer) or function(const Value: TCustomer): Boolean with begin/end and the cursor in the body. The parameters Arg1, Arg2 of the generic RTL types are named Value or after their type, with the parameter prefix of the project. After "(" the skeleton appears by itself. Off: no skeleton. |
| `completion.withOrigin` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Mark members of the with object in with blocks: label "from qryOrders" (for nested with the innermost matching object, like the compiler), and if the member hides a local name or a member of Self of the same name, the warning label "hides Self.Name" with warning background. The detail panel names both meanings. Off: members without origin. |
| `completion.exceptionClasses` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | After "raise " and "on E: " only offer exception classes. After raise project classes before library classes, accepted as EFoo.Create('') with the cursor between the quotes, plus one entry EFoo.CreateFmt per class. After "on E: " first the group "From the try block" with the classes from <exception cref> of the routines called there (and known RTL cases such as StrToInt → EConvertError), below "General"; classes already handled in the same except are missing, classes an earlier branch already catches carry the warning "never reached". Off: the ordinary list. |
| `completion.syntaxNotice` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Notice for incomplete code: if there is a syntax error before the cursor in the current routine or class declaration, the list shows the warning bar "Results may be incomplete · syntax error in line n" at the top; clicking the line number jumps there. Without suggestions the empty state shows the error. Errors in other routines and the place being typed do not count. Off: no notice. |
| `completion.sameNameVariants` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | If a name occurs in several units, show each variant with its unit; the variant the compiler picks according to uses (last unit wins) comes first with "active", the detail panel names all units declaring the name. Off: only the active variant. |
| `completion.sameNameInsert` | global (settings.json) | string | `"prefix"` | `"prefix"`, `"uses"` | Accepting a variant that is not active: prefix inserts the unit prefix (Vcl.Graphics.TBitmap), uses moves the unit to the back of its uses list or adds it; the detail panel then warns that other places may change their meaning. |
| `completion.showFmxUnits` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Show variants from FireMonkey units (FMX.*). Off: the footer names them as hidden. |
| `completion.nameSuggestions` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | At the name position of a declaration with known type (var section, inline var, field, parameter) suggest names from the type: TCustomerList gives Customers, CustomerList and List, with F, A or L if at least 60 % of the declarations of that kind in the project carry the prefix or the project file .atlas sets it under naming. |
| `completion.typeGuards` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Offer the members of the checked type after a type check: in the then branch of if X is T then (also in and chains and after while X is T do) and after if not (X is T) then Exit; up to the end of the block, X. lists the members only T has at the top under the heading "X is T here (is check, line n)". Accepting writes the cast according to completion.senderCast (T(X).Name or (X as T).Name). After an assignment to X, after passing it to a var or out parameter, in the else branch, in with blocks and for fields after any further statement the check no longer applies. After X is and X as the descendants of the type of X come first. Off: as without the check. |
| `completion.hiddenMembers` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Name members that are missing only because of their visibility: if the text typed after X. matches private, strict private, strict protected or (outside descendants) protected members, the footer names them with visibility and class ("1 match not visible: FEntries (private in TAtlasUsage) · Ctrl+Space shows it"). Pressing Ctrl+Space again shows them greyed out in the list; they are not inserted. No notice without a typed prefix. Off: left out silently as before. |
| `completion.projectFrequency` | global (settings.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Ranking from usage in the project: after X. members whose name occurs often in the project's units move up and carry the tag "in project 214×". The count comes from the index usages (index.usages); libraries do not count. Your own weighting (recent, frequent) and a better match always come first. Off: only by match and your own weighting as before. |

## refactoring

| Key | Place | Type | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `refactoring.inlineVar` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Generate inline variables (for var Item in …, var Name := …) if the Delphi version supports them (10.3 and later). Off: Atlas adds the variable to the var section of the routine. |
| `refactoring.changeSignature` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Change signature …": add, remove, reorder and rename parameters including callers, overrides, interfaces and bound events. |
| `refactoring.newParameter` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"overload"` | `"overload"`, `"updateCallers"` | New parameters: overload keeps the old signature as an overload that passes on the given value (callers stay); updateCallers changes all callers. Interface methods and bound handlers only work with updateCallers. Atlas never generates default values. |
| `refactoring.virtualOverload` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Also make the overload with the old signature virtual for virtual methods. |
| `refactoring.syncSignatures` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | If declaration and implementation differ, offer the actions "Align implementation with declaration" and vice versa. |
| `refactoring.forwardDeclaration` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Report types used in the type section before their declaration and offer "Add forward declaration", "Merge type blocks" or "Move declaration up"; report superfluous forward declarations. |
| `refactoring.propertyFromAccessors` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions "Create property X" on an accessor method and "Create missing properties (n)" on the header line of a class: for methods such as GetX/SetX (also indexed, IsX/HasX for Boolean) without property X Atlas creates the property, with read FX if the getter only returns the field. Preview before applying. |
| `refactoring.propertyFromAccessorsPrefixes` | project (atlas.json) | array<string> | `["Get","Set","Is","Has"]` |  | Prefixes of the accessor methods. Is and Has only apply to getters returning Boolean, Get only to getters, Set only to setters, your own prefixes to both. |
| `refactoring.propertyFromAccessorsReplaceCalls` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"ask"` | `"ask"`, `"always"`, `"never"` | Switch calls in the whole project to the property (X.GetCaption → X.Caption, X.SetCaption(V) → X.Caption := V); passing as method pointer stays. ask: offer both actions, with and without switching; always: always switch; never: never. |
| `refactoring.propertyFromAccessorsSection` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"accessor"` | `"accessor"`, `"public"`, `"published"` | Section of the new property: accessor like the most visible accessor method, public or published at least there. |
| `refactoring.propertyFromAccessorsHideAccessors` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"off"` | `"off"`, `"private"`, `"protected"` | After creating, move accessor methods to private or protected if they are no longer used outside their class (virtual and overridden ones stay). off: never. |
| `refactoring.freeFields` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Report object fields created in the constructor (or a private method it calls) with TClass.Create that the class never frees (field-not-freed, until #918 owned-field-not-freed) and offer the code actions "Free in destructor" on the field and "Free all owned objects (n)" on the class. If the destructor is missing, Atlas creates it with override and inherited. Components with owner as well as interface and record fields are excluded; fields that are returned or passed on are reported as unclear (owned-field-free-unclear). |
| `refactoring.freeFieldsStyle` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"free"` | `"free"`, `"freeAndNil"` | Form of freeing in the destructor: free writes FField.Free, freeAndNil writes FreeAndNil(FField). |
| `refactoring.suggestConst` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Light bulb "Declare as constant" on a variable that is assigned exactly once and never changed: var X := … becomes const X = …, a variable from the var section with a single assignment in the body becomes an inline constant with its type at that place (const X: T = …) and disappears from the var section. Only if the language version supports inline constants (Delphi 10.3 and later). Counterpart of the underline of reassigned variables in the plugin (highlight.reassigned). |
| `refactoring.invertBoolean` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Invert meaning (X → Y)" on a Boolean variable, field, constant, property, parameter or Boolean function of the project: new name with the opposite meaning, every place negated so that the program stays the same (X := True → Y := False, if not X → if Y, X = False → Y). Functions return the opposite in the body, properties take field, getter, setter and default along, overrides and interfaces follow. Preview with warnings (var/out arguments, @X, strings for RTTI), one undo step per file. |
| `refactoring.invertBooleanAntonyms` | project (atlas.json) | object | `{}` |  | Your own pairs of opposites for the name suggestion, e.g. {"Verbose": "Silent"}; they apply in both directions and before the built-in ones (Hidden ↔ Visible, Enabled ↔ Disabled, IsEmpty ↔ HasItems, Valid ↔ Invalid, Locked ↔ Unlocked …). |
| `refactoring.invertBooleanFallbackPrefix` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"Not"` |  | Prefix if no pair of opposites fits: FReady → FNotReady, IsReady → IsNotReady; an existing prefix is dropped (IsNotReady → IsReady). |
| `refactoring.invertBooleanIncludeDfm` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Also invert published properties in the forms (.dfm, .fmx) of the class and its descendants: name and value (Hidden = True → Visible = False); the default of the property is inverted too. Off: forms stay, the preview warns. |
| `refactoring.ifCase` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions "Convert to case" on an if chain that compares the same ordinal expression without side effects with constants (X = a, X in [a, b..c], (X >= a) and (X <= b), joined with or), and "Convert to if chain" on a case. Comments in the branches stay, begin … end only for several statements. The notice on long convertible if chains is the rule prefer-case. |
| `refactoring.conditions` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions to reshape conditions: "Invert condition" (swap then and else, condition negated readably: flip comparisons, De Morgan in the same order), "Introduce early exit" (if without else at the end of a routine or loop becomes if … then Exit or Continue), "Merge nested if" (if A then if B → if A and B) and "Remove double negation". Parentheses only where precedence requires them; comments in the branches stay. |
| `refactoring.conditionalExpression` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions between if statement and conditional expression (Delphi 13: X := if C then A else B): "Convert to conditional expression" on an if with else whose branches assign to the same target, call Exit or make the same call with exactly one different argument without side effects (up to two conditions, compatible types), "Convert to if statement" as the way back and "Replace IfThen with conditional expression" (IfThen evaluates both branches). If the project must compile with Delphi 12 or older, only the way back is offered; existing conditional expressions are then reported by the rule conditional-expression-version. |
| `refactoring.nestedRoutine` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions between local routine and method: "Convert to private method" or "Extract from routine" on the header of a local routine (used variables and parameters of the outer routine become parameters, var when written, const for strings, records and interfaces; constants move along), "Embed as local routine" or "Convert to local routine" on a private, non-virtual method or a free routine of the implementation with exactly one call, optionally without passed-through parameters. Each action first shows the new signature and the number of changed calls. If the local routine lies in another one, there is a notice instead of the action. |
| `refactoring.promoteVariable` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions between local variable and field: "Convert to field" on a local or inline variable of a method (suggestion F + name without L prefix, editable; the field goes after the last field of the private section, an initialization stays as assignment, the type of an inline variable without type is inferred; warning if the object is created and freed in the method) and "Convert to local variable" on a private field used by only one method that writes it first on every path (not for property, published, form field). A preview first, one undo step. |
| `refactoring.anonymousMethod` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions between anonymous method and method: "Convert to method" on the header of an anonymous method (private method of the class, in free routines a routine of the unit; name from the context such as HandleClick or CompareByName, editable). Without captured variables the method name goes in its place; captured variables become parameters (var if written), and a short anonymous forwarder calls the method with them. "Embed as anonymous method" on a private method that is passed exactly once as a value to a reference to and never called (not for events of the form file). A preview first, one undo step. |
| `refactoring.anonymousMethodDeferredCapture` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"forward"` | `"forward"`, `"fields"` | If an anonymous method with captured variables runs later (TThread.Queue, TTask.Run, event): forward leaves a short anonymous forwarder that keeps holding the variables (behavior stays the same); fields copies the values into fields before the statement and inserts the method name (the method does not see later changes; only in methods without written variables). |
| `refactoring.methodKind` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Detect methods without Self (no field, no property, no instance method, no Self, not even implicitly; not virtual/override, not an event in the form file, not a method pointer, not part of an interface) and convert them: "Convert to class method" (optionally also calls via instances to TClass.X), "Convert to free routine" (calls lose the object reference, uses in other units) and "Move to record helper" (first parameter of a simple type becomes Self, calls S.X; warning if a helper for the type is already visible). A preview with all changed calls first, one undo step per file. The hint diagnostic for this is the rule method-without-self. |
| `refactoring.methodKindMarker` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Label "Self unused" at the header of such methods; off = the actions only via Ctrl+. |
| `refactoring.methodKindStatic` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | "Convert to class method" sets static (without the hidden Self of the class); always for records. |
| `refactoring.typeAlias` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions "Introduce type alias" on a type expression (generic type with arguments, array, set, method reference, procedural type): writes X = expression into the type section before the first use (with a forward declaration of the own class if needed, in the project into the interface part) and replaces the place, all equal expressions of the unit or the project; equal means equal resolved types. Open generic parameters (TList<T> in TBox<T>) give no alias, the action names the reason. Plus "Resolve alias" on the name of an alias X = Y: replaces the uses with Y (arrays, sets and procedural types only where Delphi accepts a type expression) and removes the alias if no use remains; X = type Y stays. A preview with all places first, one undo step per file. |
| `refactoring.typeAliasScope` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"unit"` | `"here"`, `"unit"`, `"project"` | Scope of the first action "Introduce type alias": here only replaces the place, unit all equal expressions of the unit, project also the units using the unit. The other two scopes are offered as separate actions next to it. |
| `refactoring.enumTables` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions for tables over enumerations (array[TType] of …): "Create name table" on an enumeration type without fixed values writes const CTypeNames: array[TType] of string after the type (or into the implementation part) with texts from the element names (common lowercase prefix removed, CamelCase split: osPaymentDue → 'Payment due'); the name is editable. On a table whose entries no longer match the type, "Add missing entry" or "Remove surplus entry" at the right place (detected by texts, identifiers and comments such as {osPaid}; otherwise estimated and labelled so). "Update tables of TType" changes all tables over the type in the project and adds missing branches to case statements without else, with preview. |
| `refactoring.enumTablesResourceStrings` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | "Create name table" writes one resourcestring per element (translatable) and a table array[TType] of PResStringRec with @ references; read with LoadResString(CTypeNames[X]). |
| `refactoring.overloads` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions on the header of a routine (Ctrl+.): "Create overload (copy)" copies declaration and body directly after the original, both with overload; then placeholder mode first leads through the parameter list of the copy (same in declaration and implementation), then through the body. "Create overload (as forwarder)" creates an overload without the last parameter that calls the existing one and passes the default value of its type for it (0, '', False, nil, first element of an enumeration, otherwise Default(Type)), as placeholder. virtual, override, dynamic and message are not carried over to the new overload; if the original is an override, Atlas points this out. The /// comment is copied too. Merging overloads into default parameters is deliberately not offered. |
| `refactoring.varBlock` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions around local variables (Ctrl+.): "Convert to inline variable" on a variable of the var section (at the first assignment as var X := …, otherwise as var X: T; before the first use, only from Delphi 10.3 and only if all uses lie in the same or an inner block, not in anonymous methods), "Move to var block" on an inline variable (type for var X := … from the expression) and "Clean up var block" in the var section (remove unused variables, sort, merge equal types). Comments on variables move along. |
| `refactoring.varBlockMerge` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | "Clean up var block" merges consecutive variables of the same type (I, J: Integer). Off: each variable on its own line. Entries with comments and types without names (array of …) stay as they are. |
| `refactoring.varBlockSort` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"usage"` | `"usage"`, `"alpha"`, `"none"` | Order after "Clean up var block": usage by first use in the routine, alpha alphabetical, none as before. |
| `refactoring.extractInterface` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Extract interface from TFoo …" on the header line of a class: a dialog shows the public and published methods and properties to tick (all public methods preselected), the name (I + class name without T) and the target (same unit, a unit of the project or a new one). The interface gets a new GUID, the signatures with doc comments and the properties; if a property reads a field, Atlas creates Get and Set methods. The class gets the interface in its ancestor list (TInterfacedObject instead of TObject). Preview before applying. |
| `refactoring.extractSuperclass` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Extract base class …" on the header line of a class: a dialog shows fields, methods and properties to tick, for each method move or declare abstract, the name and the target (same unit above the class or a new unit). The new class inherits from the previous ancestor, the class from it; statements in constructor or destructor for moved fields move along, private members the class still uses are raised. Preview before applying. |
| `refactoring.extractSuperclassTarget` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"sameUnit"` | `"sameUnit"`, `"newUnit"` | Default for the target in the dialog: sameUnit (above the class) or newUnit (new unit with the class name without T). |
| `refactoring.extractSuperclassNameSuffix` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"Base"` |  | Suffix for the suggested name (TPdfExport → TExportBase); Custom becomes a prefix (TCustomExport). |
| `refactoring.extractSuperclassMethodMode` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"move"` | `"move"`, `"abstract"` | Default per method: move (body moves along) or abstract (virtual; abstract; above, override below). |
| `refactoring.extractSuperclassRaiseVisibility` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"protected"` | `"protected"`, `"strictProtected"` | Visibility for private members that move to the base class and are still used below. |
| `refactoring.moveMember` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions "Move "Run" to ancestor …" and "Move "Run" to descendants …" on a field, method or property: a dialog shows the members to tick (used ones to take along), the target (ancestors or direct descendants in the project), upwards per method move or declare abstract and whether methods of the same name in other descendants become override, downwards whether the methods stay abstract in the ancestor. If foreign code uses the member via the ancestor type, Atlas forbids moving down. Private members become protected if needed, missing uses are added. Preview before applying. |
| `refactoring.inlineAccessor` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Replace accessor GetName with field FName" on a property and on a trivial accessor method: if a getter only returns a field (Result := FName;) or a setter only sets a field (FName := Value;), the property then points directly to the field, declaration and body are removed. Only for methods that are not virtual, implement no interface, have no index and are never called directly (reference search). Preview before applying. |
| `refactoring.inlineAccessorEqualityCheck` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Setters with equality check (if FName <> Value then FName := Value;) count as trivial. Setters with notification (Changed, Invalidate) never. |
| `refactoring.inlineAccessorBulk` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Also the bulk actions "Replace all trivial accessors of the unit (n)" and "… of the project" with preview; methods with calls stay, the preview names them. |
| `refactoring.inlineAccessorDiagnostic` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Hint diagnostic trivial-accessor on trivial accessor methods (severity adjustable via the rule); the light bulb on the message replaces them. |
| `refactoring.raiseVisibility` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Raise visibility of X to protected/public" on the declaration of a field, method or property: the declaration moves with its doc comment into the protected or public section, which is created if needed; the implementation stays. Not for published and not in the first section without keyword (form fields). Code completion offers the action for members that are not visible regardless of this setting. |
| `refactoring.safeDelete` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | "Safe delete" (Alt+Del in the editor, code action "Safely delete method "Run" …") for methods (overloads individually), fields, properties, types, constants, global variables, routines, local routines and, on the line "unit X;", for the whole unit. Atlas first searches for uses in the project, in forms (events, components), in uses lists, overrides and interface implementations. Without uses it deletes at once, otherwise a list shows the places (Cancel, Show, Delete anyway). Doc comment and attributes go along, empty sections are removed. |
| `refactoring.safeDeletePreviewWhenUnused` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Show the preview first even without uses instead of deleting at once. |
| `refactoring.safeDeleteCascade` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"ask"` | `"ask"`, `"always"`, `"never"` | What becomes unused by deleting (private fields and methods, getter and setter of a property, uses entries): ask, always (delete too) or never (leave in place). |
| `refactoring.safeDeleteIncludeOverrides` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"ask"` | `"ask"`, `"always"`, `"never"` | Overrides of a virtual method in descendants: ask, always (delete too) or never (count as use). |
| `refactoring.tryFinally` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Add try/finally" after X := TFoo.Create(…) for local variables (for Result: try/except that only frees on failure). The try block encloses the following statements up to the end of the block or the end of the selection. |
| `refactoring.classActions` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions in a class declaration: "Generate getter, setter and field" on a property without read/write, "Implement methods of IFoo" and "Override Name" for virtual methods of the ancestors. |
| `refactoring.explicitType` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Write out type" on the name of var X := …, const X = … and for var X in … without type: inserts the inferred type (var Count: Integer := Lines.Count) and adds its unit to uses if needed. |
| `refactoring.compilerFixes` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Quick fixes on messages of the last compiler run: H2443 adds the unit from the message to uses, E2003 offers the units declaring the identifier (RTL and VCL first), H2077 removes an ineffective assignment (for a call only the call stays), W1035 inserts Result := Default(<Type>); at the start of the function, W1057/W1058 add an explicit cast (string(…), AnsiString(…)). If the same message occurs several times in the file, also "Fix all … in the file". Each fix is one undo step. |
| `refactoring.missingUnit` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions on "Unit not found" (F2613, F1026) of the last compiler run: Atlas searches the unit in the project folder and its subfolders, in the other projects of the group, in the search paths of the other configurations and platforms, in the library paths of other platforms and in the index. For a hit: "Add folder to the search path of this configuration", "… of all configurations" (relative to the .dproj, via the project options of the IDE) and, for a source, "Add unit to project". If the unit only exists for other platforms, the action says so ("Winapi.Windows does not exist for Linux64"); without a hit it names the searched places. |
| `refactoring.disableWarning` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions on a warning or hint of the last compiler run: "Disable W1000 here" puts {$WARN SYMBOL_DEPRECATED OFF} before and {$WARN SYMBOL_DEPRECATED ON} after the line, plus variants around the routine, for the whole unit and (after asking) for the whole project in the project options. Hints get {$HINTS OFF}/{$HINTS ON}, warnings without their own identifier {$WARNINGS OFF}/{$WARNINGS ON} (affects all warnings). Flow messages such as H2164 or W1035 only around the whole routine. One undo step. |
| `refactoring.disableWarningReason` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Ask for a reason when disabling a warning; it goes as a comment after the switch ({$WARN SYMBOL_DEPRECATED OFF} // legacy until migration). Empty allowed. Off: no question, no comment. |
| `refactoring.extract` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code actions "Extract method" (selected statements become a new method or routine; parameters by data flow: only read const, written and then read var or out, only inside local variable), "Introduce variable" (also for all textually equal occurrences in the block) and "Extract constant" (in the routine or in the unit). Inline variable or var section according to inlineVar. |
| `refactoring.extractMethodDuplicates` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | For "Extract method" the second action "Extract method and replace equal places": it searches all routines of the unit for statement sequences that are textually equal to the selection (comments, whitespace and case do not count) and replaces them with the same call. A place is only offered if the same new method would result there: same class or level, same meaning of the names, same parameter list by data flow; not in with bodies. The preview lists the places for deselecting. |
| `refactoring.completeCase` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Complete case": for case over an enumeration type adds exactly the missing values as empty branches in declaration order. With else it is called "Add missing values before else" and is not the preferred action. |
| `refactoring.resolveWith` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Code action "Resolve with": identifiers in the with body that belong to a member of a with expression get that expression prepended (innermost element first); costly expressions of class type first go into a local variable. If an identifier cannot be resolved unambiguously, the action is not offered. |
| `refactoring.inline` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | **Experimental (off by default; only active with `experimental.enabled`).** Code actions "Inline variable" and "Inline method" on a local variable or a call: the variable disappears, its places get the expression; the call is replaced by the body (local names renamed uniquely, arguments substituted or put into helper variables, members with the receiver, the result directly or in a variable such as AddResult). Only offered if data flow and name resolution show that the meaning does not change. Helper variables as inline variable or in the var section according to refactoring.inlineVar. |
| `refactoring.moveClass` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | **Experimental (off by default; only active with `experimental.enabled`).** Code action "Move class to its own unit …" on the first line of a class or record declaration: the declaration with attributes, comment and method bodies goes into a new unit next to the old one (name from the class name without T, editable in the dialog). The new unit is then listed in .dpr or .dpk and .dproj; its uses are built from the names needed, and all units using the class include it. Not offered for access to names from the implementation part of the old unit, circular reference, form classes and conditional compilation. |
| `refactoring.unitRenameFollowUp` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"off"` | `"ask"`, `"off"` | **Experimental (off by default; only active with `experimental.enabled`).** After renaming a unit in the project manager (the IDE only updates .dpr and .dproj) Atlas reports in the notification center how many units still use the old name and offers to update uses entries and qualified identifiers (Old.TClass) in the project or in the project group, with preview and undoable. ask: offer; off: off. |
| `refactoring.createMethod` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `true` |  | Create method from call: after "(" behind an unknown name and with Ctrl+Space on such a call Atlas offers to create the method (inside a method of the class) or free routine; for Obj.Name(…) in the class of Obj, if it belongs to the project (also as a code action). Parameter types from the arguments, return type from the assignment or the expected type; without assignment a procedure. |
| `refactoring.createMethodSection` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"private"` | `"private"`, `"protected"`, `"public"` | Section of the new method if the class is in the same unit. In another unit it always goes to public so that the call compiles. |

| `format.beginPlacement` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"newLine"`, `"sameLine"` | begin after then, else and do: as existing, on its own line or on the same line. |
| `format.elsePlacement` | project (atlas.json) | string | `"preserve"` | `"preserve"`, `"newLine"`, `"sameLine"` | else after end: as existing, on its own line or on the same line (end else). |
| `format.maxLineLength` | project (atlas.json) | integer | `0` | 0…1000 | Wrap longer lines after a comma or before an operator; 0 = never. When set it takes precedence over max_line_length from .editorconfig. |
| `format.alignAssignments` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Align := of assignments on consecutive lines. |
| `format.alignDeclarations` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Align colons or = of declarations on consecutive lines (var, const, fields, parameters). |
| `format.alignComments` | project (atlas.json) | boolean | `false` |  | Align end-of-line comments of consecutive lines. |

## issues

| Key | Place | Type | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `issues.connections` | global (settings.json) | array<object> | `` |  | Personal tracker connections (#1260), e.g. the company YouTrack and GitHub side by side. The token is never stored here but in the Windows credential store (Atlas:tracker:<server>, "Store token …"). |
| `issues.projects` | global (settings.json) | array<object> | `` |  | Personal mapping Delphi project → tracker project (#1261) for projects without tracker in the .atlas. The line for exactly this .dproj applies, otherwise the one for the open .groupproj, otherwise the longest matching folder; an .atlas with tracker takes precedence. |
| `issues.queries` | global (settings.json) | array<object> | `` |  | Named queries for "My issues" (#1262), selectable in the drop-down next to the title. Without own queries "Assigned to me" applies per provider (GitHub assignee:@me state:open, YouTrack for: me #Unresolved). An earlier issues.query becomes the query "Default" once. |

## Example

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xKnockOut/Atlas-IDE-Expert/main/schemas/atlas.schema.json",
  "project": "App.dproj",
  "config": "Debug",
  "platform": "Win64",
  "rules": { "empty-except": "error" },
  "exclude": ["ThirdParty/**"]
}
```
